You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure arises from an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in Base64.encode called from Base64InputStream.read after many sequential read() calls on an encoding Base64InputStream. The test calls read() and expects safe incremental encoding.

The Base64InputStream.read() method (lines 108-117) internally reads bytes into a one-byte buffer using the read(byte[],int,int) method. If that method returns zero, it retries until a non-zero read happens or EOF (-1).

Looking at Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) method (lines 138-182), it contains a while-loop that continues to read from the underlying stream into an intermediate buffer until Base64 data is available (base64.hasData()). When data is ready, it calls either base64.encode() or base64.decode() on this buffer depending on a flag. It then returns decoded/encoded results from base64.readResults().

The Base64.encode method (lines 444-508) manages an internal buffer and state variables to perform encoding. It uses a modulus to track how many bytes have been processed mod 3 and accumulates bits in 'x' to map to 4 Base64 output bytes. At EOF (inAvail < 0), the method outputs padding bytes and finalizes the buffer. During encoding, bytes are shifted into 'x' and when modulus reaches 0, it outputs 4 encoded bytes.

The issue is likely caused by an inconsistency or corruption in state variables 'modulus', 'pos', or the buffer array in Base64.encode when handling continuous byte-by-byte reads and encoding in Base64InputStream. The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException happens because the buffer position 'pos' is incremented past the buffer length somewhere in the encode method, specifically at the lines like buffer[pos++] = encodeTable[(x >> ...)]. This likely means the buffer is not resized appropriately or the 'pos' and 'modulus' counters are out of sync.

Because Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) repeatedly feeds small portions into Base64.encode, but Base64.encode expects to accumulate 3 bytes before producing output, the modulus logic and buffer resizing must correctly handle small incremental calls. The bug likely manifests after many incremental reads such that a buffer is too small or the encoding state is corrupted leading to pos exceeding the buffer limits.

The test triggers this by doing multiple read() calls one byte at a time on an encoding Base64InputStream wrapping a custom error input stream, leading to this buffer overflow and exception.

In summary, the root cause is an off-by-one or capacity management bug in Base64.encode's buffer handling during incremental encoding of an input stream in Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int). This causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when buffer 'pos' is incremented beyond its size due to incorrect resizing or state tracking of 'modulus' and 'pos'.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)
